newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P rates Eastern Energy note issue A-minus.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P rates Eastern Energy note issue A-minus.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday it had assigned its A-minus rating to Eastern Energy's US$350 million, two-part Rule 144A debt issue.
S&P said the first part of the issue consisted of US$250 million 10-year notes with a coupon rate of 6.75 percent and maturity date of December 1, 2006.
The second part consisted of US$100 million 20-year notes with a coupon rate of 7.25 percent maturing on December 1, 2016.
The rating outlook was stable, S&P said.
Eastern Energy is an electricity distributor and retailer operating in the Australian state of Victoria.

"Its rating reflects the stable regulatory regime under which the utility operates, the diversity of its customer base and service area, and the natural monopoly characteristics of Eastern Energy's franchise network business," S&P said.
"These factors are offset somewhat by its modest financial profile," the credit rating agency said.
